what_this_is: The Workshop rows for screen looks: resolve a supplied look for documents, and read the person's current worn look and schedule as native device tokens through the person's records door.

payload.label: Read my current screen look
payload.job: Read this person's current worn screen look, look rules and day plan as the device token payload native screens draw
payload.description: Reads this person's current worn screen look and returns the token payload native screens draw: every wearable look, the look now (including a scheduled blend), upcoming changes for twelve hours, and when to read again. `app_data` is the calling app owner's current look DATA: its starting look and themes, plan anchors/presets, and rule facts. Those values are supplied at runtime, never chosen by this generic reader. time_zone is required and must be an IANA zone. host, device, device_id and place are the facts this native screen says about itself; only saved rules matching those facts select another look. A missing personal choice uses `app_data.looks.start_with`. A workspace refusal or unverified answer is an error, never an empty record. Returns `{ worn, worn_record, now, ahead, looks, read_again_at }` in the DeviceLooks token format.

time_zone.description: The native device's IANA time zone, such as America/Denver

host.description: The app or place where the native screen is drawn, from the saved look rules' hosts

device.description: The device kind, from the saved look rules' devices

device_id.description: The particular device id, when the native host has one

place.description: The screen or area of the app, when the native host knows it

provenance.source: src/looks.mjs device(), src/workspace/inputs.json and parts/screen-look/read-data; generic reader consumes app-owned look, schedule and rule DATA supplied by its caller

payload.label: Resolve a look
payload.job: Turn a look's colour, size and font tokens into concrete values and the stylesheet a document carries, with the person's own font faces
payload.description: Give a request file: look (the look record as its owner keeps it: tokens of {key, value, css_variable?}) and faces (the person's own font files: family, weight, style, file, relative to the request). Answers the look's concrete values by variable name (--accent-primary, --font-display and the rest), the font families the look names, which faces were written and which files were missing; with --css it writes one stylesheet: a @font-face for each named face, then the look's variables. Nothing about a colour or a font is in the tool: the look and the faces decide.

request.description: The request JSON file: {look, faces?}, put where {request} is in the command.

css.description: Where to write the stylesheet, put where {css} is in the command.

invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer, from the root of the Workshop checkout. Write the request with the look record and the person's own font files, run `run`, then tell the person the look's main colours and fonts and any face file that was missing. If the command exits 2, its standard error says what to change. If you cannot run commands, give them these steps.

provenance.source: The look resolver the account screens wear: one token-to-value resolver for every surface, plus the stylesheet a document carries itself
